tasks.short: Oversee regional sales managers, resolve operating problems, and agree support and staffing priorities.

steps.what: Review regional pipelines, results, and overdue customer commitments
Send staffing constraints, support requests, and unresolved team issues
Prepare the regional review agenda
Discuss performance, coach managers, and understand local constraints
Agree resource changes, escalation owners, and management actions
Record agreed actions, owners, and due dates
Check progress and chase overdue actions

tasks.design: Configure regional exception views in the {CRM} and structured manager updates in the {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic generator assembles a review agenda in the {DOCS}, retaining managers' comments verbatim and linking each figure to its source. Approved actions create records in the {PROJECT}, with reminders and overdue exceptions sent through the {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational figures, local context, and action status sit in separate places. Someone must maintain shared definitions and the joins between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting, forms, and reminder features cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort needed for the remaining joins and agenda generator.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching, competing regional priorities, and sensitive staffing decisions remain human. Employee data access and consultation obligations depend on the proposed use and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what a local manager is reluctant to say, challenge explanations fairly, and negotiate support across regions.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less report preparation and more coaching and removal of cross-region obstacles. Formal staffing and budget decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan short-term coverage for customer handovers and specialist support
reach.learn: Learn workload estimation, coverage constraints, and the supervisor's escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Structured updates, template assembly, and action reminders can use deterministic technology; coaching remains human.
Pipedrive provides deal probability and next-action support, establishing available pipeline components rather than automated staff supervision.
The step shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured customer results.

assumptions: The scope is routine supervision; formal employment changes follow the existing approval process.
Action owners maintain completion status in the {PROJECT}; silence does not count as completion.
The design uses operational exceptions and does not generate employee rankings or performance scores.
GDPR applies to employee records; any later AI-based employee evaluation requires assessment under the EU AI Act and national rules.
Build ranges are working-day effort for one initial deployment; consultation and access waiting time may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Available regional reporting views and connector permissions.
Consistency of regional sales definitions and action ownership.
Required employee consultation, access restrictions, and retention periods.
research_questions: Can existing reporting and forms generate the agenda without custom integration?
Which operational exceptions warrant discussion rather than a routine notification?
new_work: Review the generated agenda before sharing.
Maintain regional definitions, exception thresholds, and access groups.
Resolve stale action records and connector failures.

tasks.short: Resolve escalated customer complaints, agree remedies, and coordinate their completion.

steps.what: Read the complaint and identify its issue, urgency, and owner

loop.input: Complaint text and attachments, with a fixed issue taxonomy and escalation rules.
loop.output: Source-linked facts, requested remedy, proposed category, and explicit uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Require source spans for extracted facts; validate category fields; a manager confirms routing and urgency.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per complaint; unreadable or ambiguous cases return to manual triage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers describe mixed issues in free text; keyword rules alone miss context and negation.

steps.what: Check the account, order history, and previous commitments
Confirm what happened and which recovery options are feasible
Hear the customer's concerns and discuss a workable resolution
Authorise a remedy within delegated limits or escalate approval
Write and send the agreed resolution and next steps

loop.input: Approved remedy, verified facts, customer priorities, and an approved response template.
loop.output: A resolution message containing only authorised commitments.
loop.check: Match amounts, dates, and promises to approved fields; the sales manager checks tone and approves sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one requested revision; unresolved factual conflicts or failed checks require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply the structure, but individual complaints need contextual acknowledgement and plain explanations.

steps.what: Coordinate delivery of the authorised remedy
Confirm acceptance or explain what remains unresolved
Record the outcome and close or reopen the complaint

tasks.design: Join the {HELPDESK} case to account and order history from the {CRM} and {ERP}, using deterministic identity checks and recovery-policy fields. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a case brief and a resolution message, with human gates on routing, remedy authorisation, sending, and closure. The {WORKFLOW} assigns recovery actions and tracks confirmation while people handle the customer conversation and disputed facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts and promises are scattered across service records and correspondence. Free-text complaints resist simple routing rules, while settlement requires clear authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case workflows and record joins handle coordination. Bounded text extraction and drafting can reduce preparation while keeping commitments tied to approved fields.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed evidence, distressed customers, legal claims, and remedies involving several teams remain difficult. Integration cannot make physical recovery work happen.
tasks.human_edge: Restore trust, recognise when a policy-compliant remedy is inadequate, and take responsibility for a credible commitment.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconstructing cases and more time resolving recurring failures with service leads. Remedy limits and formal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Investigate order amendments and delivery discrepancies before proposing recovery
reach.learn: Learn order-event evidence, amendment permissions, and credit escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Record joins, approval limits, ownership, and reminders can be deterministic; negotiated complaint resolution remains human.
HubSpot offers email drafting and outreach components; this is component evidence, not evidence of reliable complaint settlement.
A documented DPD service-chatbot failure supports keeping free-form customer responses constrained and reviewed before sending.
The time allocations and build ranges are estimates; the digest provides no measured outcome for this complaint workflow.

assumptions: This describes escalated complaints needing manager involvement, rather than routine service enquiries.
The task covers coordinating recovery; field repairs, shipment handling, and payment execution belong to their own workflows.
Any financial remedy uses the existing authorised approval route.
GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose limitation, and retention for customer records; EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed use.
No call recording or automatic transcription is assumed.
Build ranges are working-day effort; access and any consultation under national rules can add elapsed time.
unknowns: Complaint volumes, languages, and attachment formats.
Reliable account and order identifiers across systems.
Rules for closure, retention, and customer-record access.
research_questions: Which complaint categories can be routed with existing fields and rules alone?
Can brief extraction preserve uncertainty and distinguish allegations from verified facts?
Which response passages actually require contextual drafting beyond approved templates?
new_work: Review extracted facts, routing, and customer messages.
Handle identity mismatches and unresolved evidence.
Maintain remedy limits, templates, and escalation rules.
Sample completed cases for unsupported promises and premature closure.

tasks.short: Combine customer behaviour and feedback to choose where the sales team should focus.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, repeat-purchase, and win-loss data by customer segment
Retrieve campaign engagement and stated interests by customer segment
Align segments and compare customer signals over time
Read customer comments and identify recurring needs and objections

loop.input: A fixed batch of customer comments and win-loss notes, grouped by approved segment.
loop.output: Cited preference themes, objections, contradictory examples, and unclassified comments.
loop.check: Require record references; calculate counts in code; review samples and retain contradictions and missing coverage.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per batch; ambiguous comments remain unclassified for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers express the same need in different language; fixed keywords do not reliably preserve context.

steps.what: Test apparent preferences against sales representatives' customer experience
Choose segment priorities and a limited sales experiment
Publish approved sales priorities and the experiment brief

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors bring approved fields from the {CRM} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic joins and counts feed a segment dashboard in the {BI}. A bounded classifier groups customer comments with source references, while the manager validates the interpretation and chooses an experiment. A template generator publishes the approved sales focus brief in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Segment definitions and customer identifiers differ across exports. Reading feedback takes time, and engagement measures are easily mistaken for purchase preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and scheduled transformations can maintain a repeatable comparison. Bounded classification can organise text without making the final commercial judgement.
tasks.still_hard: The available customers may be unrepresentative, sales notes may omit lost buyers, and campaign engagement may reflect exposure rather than demand. Commercial experiments still need enough observations and time.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a plausible customer need from a data artefact and choose a commercially useful, testable response.
tasks.altitude: The manager can review segment evidence weekly and spend more time designing and interpreting sales experiments. With an agreed mandate, they can adjust prospecting capacity within existing budget limits.

reach.task: Run discovery interviews to test a segment-specific buying hypothesis
reach.learn: Learn neutral questioning, sampling limits, and how to distinguish stated interest from buying intent.

evidence.claim: Spotler provides lead management, predicted customer value, and campaign-data queries, supporting available customer-signal components.
The Neleman vendor case documents segmentation outcomes; it does not establish results for this sales-focus workflow.
Deterministic aggregation and bounded text classification can prepare evidence, but neither establishes causal customer demand.
Step shares, remaining time, and delivery ranges are estimates rather than customer measurements.

assumptions: The initial scope uses existing customer and campaign records, rather than commissioning a new survey.
Analysis uses approved business segments and excludes inferred sensitive personal attributes.
GDPR applies to personal data and profiling; any resulting outreach must separately meet applicable marketing rules and respect objections.
The proposed weekly cadence is an ambition, not a documented performance result.
Build ranges are working-day effort; access reviews and any consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Completeness of lost-customer and win-loss feedback.
Permitted analytical uses, retention rules, and suppression handling.
Authority to change prospecting capacity and minimum useful segment sizes.
research_questions: Do behavioural changes persist after accounting for seasonality, exposure, and customer mix?
Does text classification preserve minority needs and contradictory feedback?
Can existing reporting provide the segment comparison without a new data pipeline?
new_work: Maintain segment mappings and data-quality checks.
Review theme samples, contradictions, and unclassified comments.
Monitor access, retention, and permitted-use rules.

tasks.short: Understand customer equipment needs and recommend technically suitable purchase options.

steps.what: Review the enquiry and retrieve relevant equipment specifications
Discuss intended use, site conditions, budget, and operating constraints
Record the customer's requirements and unresolved questions

loop.input: The manager's written discovery notes and a fixed equipment-requirements schema.
loop.output: Requirement fields, source references, and explicit unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate units and ranges; cite each value; never infer missing specifications; the manager approves the record.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous values remain blank for customer clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conversational notes contain requirements in varied language; a fixed form alone would require manual re-entry.

steps.what: Compare equipment options against recorded requirements
Validate technical suitability and resolve site-specific compatibility questions
Explain suitable options, trade-offs, and the recommended purchase
Prepare the written recommendation with assumptions and technical conditions
Check and send the equipment recommendation

tasks.design: Use an indexed catalogue in the {DOCS} and a requirements record in the {CRM}, with a bounded extractor to turn written discovery notes into fields for approval. A deterministic comparison app in the {WORKFLOW} filters documented specifications, exposes missing constraints, and passes the shortlist to a sales engineer. A template generator in the {DOCS} produces the recommendation from approved fields, and the manager approves sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrive conversationally, while equipment specifications use inconsistent documents and units. Expert compatibility knowledge is often undocumented.
tasks.enabler_now: A small requirements app, unit validation, constraint rules, and document templates can now be assembled with less implementation effort. Text extraction reduces re-entry but does not establish technical suitability.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions, installation interfaces, safety implications, and undocumented product limitations still require qualified judgement. Catalogue cleaning and encoding compatibility rules may dominate the cost.
tasks.human_edge: Discover the real operating need, explain trade-offs honestly, and recognise when a site assessment or specialist is necessary.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time comparing specifications and preparing documents, leaving more time for discovery and explaining trade-offs. They can offer a site-readiness brief, while technical sign-off remains with the sales engineer and commercial authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Screen basic capacity and interface requirements before detailed engineering
reach.learn: Learn specification units, operating tolerances, compatibility limits, and mandatory engineering escalation points.

evidence.claim: Known specification constraints, unit checks, and recommendation templates can be implemented deterministically.
A bounded extractor can prepare structured requirements, but technical suitability requires validated rules and qualified review.
The digest contains no documented equipment-advisory case; time savings and build ranges here are estimates.

assumptions: This task describes a business selling equipment where the sales manager handles complex enquiries with sales-engineering support.
The initial scope covers one equipment family with maintained technical specifications.
Unknown constraints block a suitability claim rather than being treated as satisfied.
The notes extractor uses written notes; call recording and transcription are outside scope.
GDPR applies where enquiries contain personal data; applicable EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules depend on the deployed use.
Build ranges are working-day effort and exclude extensive catalogue remediation or engineering-rule discovery.
unknowns: Catalogue completeness, version control, and unit consistency.
Which compatibility constraints are documented and testable.
Required engineering sign-off and site-assessment triggers.
Access rights, customer confidentiality requirements, and permitted data processing.
research_questions: Can an existing configurator cover the equipment family before building a comparison app?
Which requirements can be captured directly in a short form, reserving extraction for free-text notes?
Can historical recommendations expose missing rules without treating past decisions as technical ground truth?
new_work: Approve extracted requirements and clarify missing values.
Maintain catalogue versions, unit mappings, and compatibility rules.
Route novel configurations to sales engineering.
Check generated recommendations against technical approval before sending.

role.altitude: The sales manager's week shifts from assembling records and chasing updates toward coaching, customer recovery, and commercial experiments. Existing employment, remedy, technical, and budget authority remains; any mandate to adjust prospecting capacity must be explicitly agreed.
reach: Sales supervisor: short-term coverage and customer handover planning.
Order clerk: evidence-based investigation of order and delivery discrepancies.
Sales representative: discovery interviews that test segment hypotheses.
Sales engineer: preliminary requirements screening within documented limits.
skills_to_grow: Define operational exceptions and test data quality.
Read segment evidence without confusing correlation with demand.
Design small sales experiments and interpret their results.
Review extracted facts and generated customer documents.
Translate technical constraints and approval limits into explicit rules.
Coach managers and negotiate recovery commitments.
role.ambitious_version: A sales manager who runs a weekly segment-focus decision, offers a pre-purchase site-readiness brief, and convenes repeat-complaint recovery reviews, supported by reliable records and explicit approval limits.
